messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: run-time requirements of stan
parts:
I was on vacation, but I'm back on my packaging r/stan for Debian
project.

Once rstan is installed on a system what does it need to operate?
In particular, does it need the boost, eigen, or stan headers?
Clearly it needs the C compiler and the stan library, though I'm a
little confused about whether it uses the static or dynamic one; both
are in the makefile.

There are actually 3 different phases:
stanc (exported as a function for rstan) creates cc source file.
the cc file produced by stanc is compiled
the compiled file is run.

I've speculated that the static and dynamic libraries might be used in
different phases, but I haven't traced it through.

This matters because Debian has two types of dependency relations,
build-depends and depends. build-depends are requirements to build the
package, which corresponds to everything through R CMD INSTALL. Then
someone on a different machine can install the binary (Debian) package
and use it. It's good to keep the depends and build-depends lists as
minimal as possible.

Ross Boylan

messages.subject: Re: run-time requirements of stan
parts:
On Saturday, August 24, 2013 5:55:17 PM UTC-4, Ross Boylan wrote:
Once rstan is installed on a system what does it need to operate?
In particular, does it need the boost, eigen, or stan headers?
All three, although not all of boost
Clearly it needs the C compiler and the stan library
C++ compiler, in particular g++ >= 4.2 or clang++ (not sure what version precisely but the clang++ in testing is adequate)
a little confused about whether it uses the static or dynamic one

There are actually 3 different phases:
stanc (exported as a function for rstan) creates cc source file
There is no run-time requirement for stanc, except maybe bash (not sure if we have tested any other shells). To build stanc various parts of boost/spirit are needed but not boost/math and so forth.
the cc file produced by stanc is compiled

This step somewhat unintuitively requires a lot of boost (and Eigen) headers but not boost/spirit . Also, libstan needs to be available at link time
 
the compiled file is run

Might require the bash shell specifically but I don't know.

This matters because Debian has two types of dependency relations,
build-depends and depends.  build-depends are requirements to build the
package, which corresponds to everything through R CMD INSTALL.  Then
someone on a different machine can install the binary (Debian) package
and use it.  It's good to keep the depends and build-depends lists as
minimal as possible.

The only case where build-depends and depends are going to differ substantially is the boost/spirit stuff that is needed to build stanc but not needed to run anything. Eigen is not needed to build stanc I don't think. In the makefile, stanc depends on libstan, but I don't know if that is actually necessary.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] run-time requirements of stan
parts:
Because bin/stanc generates code which gets compiled, the
terminology "run time" and "compile time" are relative.

Stan compiles the following three targets. The first two
are executables, so you don't need anything else once they're made:

1. bin/stanc
2. bin/print

The third is an archive, which is used later for compiling models:

3. bin/libstan.a

Then, at "run time", bin/stanc is executed and passed
a new Stan model files to generate a .cpp file for the model.

This leads to a fourth compile target.

4.a. For the command line, the model's .cpp file is compiled with a main()
and generates an executable that can then be run run.

4.b. In R, the model.cpp is compiled dynamically without a main()
method [bin/stanc is configured not to generate a main]
and then the the dynamic object file is linked in using whatever
magic Rcpp, inline and R give us.

All four compiles involve the headers for Boost and Eigen. We
probably could get away without Eigen in building bin/stanc.

- Bob
